content: The use of this medication should be tailored to your specific medical condition and how you respond to treatment. It is essential to follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Take the medication regularly as prescribed to achieve the maximum benefit. To help you remember, take it at the same time each day. Do not increase the dose or take it more frequently than directed. Continue taking the medication for the full duration of the prescribed treatment, even if you feel better. If you are using over-the-counter cimetidine for self-treatment of acid indigestion or heartburn, take one tablet orally with a glass of water as needed. To prevent heartburn, take one tablet orally with a glass of water right before or up to 30 minutes before consuming food or beverages that trigger heartburn. Do not exceed two tablets in 24 hours unless directed by your doctor. Common side effects may include headache, dizziness, drowsiness, or diarrhea. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking cimetidine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other H2 blockers (such as famotidine, nizatidine, or ranitidine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Some symptoms may indicate a more serious condition. Liquid forms of this medication may contain sugar and/or alcohol, so caution is advised if you have diabetes, liver disease, or any condition requiring dietary restrictions. This drug may cause dizziness or drowsiness, and alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, particularly confusion and lung infections (such as pneumonia). During pregnancy, cimetidine should only be used when clearly necessary, as it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cimetidine can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. Additionally, by reducing stomach acid, cimetidine may alter the absorption of certain medications, impacting their effectiveness. Examples of affected drugs include atazanavir, dasatinib, certain azole antifungals (such as itraconazole and ketoconazole), levoketoconazole, pazopanib, and sparsentan, among others. Cigarette smoking can also affect this medication. Cimetidine and similar H2 blockers (such as famotidine, nizatidine, and ranitidine) are available with or without a prescription. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Lifestyle changes, such as stress reduction programs, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol intake, and dietary modifications (e.g., avoiding caffeine and spicy foods), may enhance the effectiveness of this medication. Your doctor may recommend lab tests or medical evaluations while you are taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
